Flake and Chips- Aussies take a bite out of our sharks

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
“Flake and Chips- Aussies take a bite out of our sharks” Sharks are protected in Australia so they importing ours for what they call “flake and chips

Summary:
Demersal long liners are catching sharks, mostly Bronze and Copper sharks but also hammer heads which are protected and exporting them to Australia and Shark Fin mainly to Japan. In 2018 SA exported 113 tons of shark fin to Asia and 56 tons of shark meat. Shark fin is dried before export so you can imagine how many more sharks are being killed. The DEA is not issuing quotas on the number of sharks that fishermen can catch, and despite their own fisheries scientist warning them of the huge drop in numbers the long liners are stripping our waters of shark.

27 of the 30 sharks tagged in PE were caught by a single demersal long line vessel. They have fished out the sharks around PE so have moved to just outside De Hoop Marine protected area. With the demise of the Great Whites, not only due to the Orcas but the demise of the smaller sharks the shark diving tour operators in Gansbaai have paid nearly R1 million rand to local fishermen not catch Bronze/Copper sharks off Gansbaai “watching” zone so they can keep the shark cage diving afloat. But in the last few months this ”deal” has broken down and more and more boats are coming in from Cape Town and catching sharks right in front of tourists.

40 Bronze Whalers were taken out two weeks ago. a month ago fishermen came right up to a shark cage diving boat and caught 4 bronze whaler sharks. A video of 40 smooth-hound sharks and about 12 dozen soupfin sharks and 6 hammerheads was taken just off De Hoop. Sharks reproduce slowly and the copper and hammer heads are listed as endangered species. Over 1 Million sharks are killed annually and not only is this destroying the oceans ecology it’s destroying a local tourist industry, in 2016 we had 85 000 shark cage diving tourist its dropped to below 50 000 now- they say a live shark supports five jobs for every 1 job a dead shark, it’s an industry that employs over 300 local people.

Further information:
Recently the shark cage diving fraternity met with the DEA and shared their research and feel like some progress has been made. But on the other front a dermisal longliner heads back to PE to unload their catch and will be greeted by local inspectors and conservationists - we have a film crew on standby to document it

We will also speak to local fishermen who complain about the impact of the longliners and why they resort to catching copper sharks.

Covid 19 will impact the local shark cage diving industry massively and Gansbaai operators are concerned that if they are not out on the water the monitoring work they do of the great whites and other sharks will be severely impacted and it will be open season for people who wont be monitored by conservation and shark cage diving operators

Extra Budget Items:
Gansbaai is a 3 hour drive from Cape Town and we have to interview Chris Fallow in Cape Town so will need an additional half day to accommodate the distances

Script:


Script: Great White sharks haven’t been spotted in False Bay for the last two years, they’ve all but disappeared, leaving scientists at odds to the reasons why.
Link: The Aussies are taking a bite out of our local shark population, we are exporting shark caught off South African waters to feed the Australian fast food market and our scientists say that it’s literally taking the food out of our great whites mouths
Script: It’s called Flake and chips, and before lockdown it was extremely popular, says Australian shark conservationist Dr Leonardo Guida, but strangely many people don’t even know they’re eating shark even although the texture is very different.
Leonardo: it still surprises me how many people aren’t actually aware of exactly what Flake is it's just accepted that it's fish and coming from Australia
Link: Globally 30% of sharks and rays are threatened with extinction, in South Africa we have seen the dramatic decline in Great Whites in False Bay and Gansbaai and local scientists are linking this to just one fishery.
Script: World renowned wildlife photographer Chris Fallows took the iconic flying shark images, and has spent the last 25 years working with them
Chris “ What I think has led to the drastic reduction in great whites has been a huge overfishing of their primary prey species, which are actually smaller sharks for 80 per cent of their life history Great whites are heavily reliant on these smaller shark species. So what I could liken it to is if your supermarket stopped stocking your primary foodstuffs, so milk and bread and that sort of thing, you'd go look elsewhere
Script: Some believe that orca whales which hunt Great Whites were the reason they fled.
Chris ”The orcas are a sexy sideshow to what's really happening [15:54:45] We know that when the orcas come into an area, great whites certainly in the Gansbaai area and Mossel Bay areas leave for periods leave for up to two months at a time. So there is a short to medium term effect. However, the complete absence of great whites cannot be related to that.
Script: In the late 90’s in South Africa a new fishery was introduced called demersal shark long lining, which catches shark that live and feed at the bottom of coastal areas. It's a very small fishing sector with only 5 rights holders. They target mainly Soupfin and Smoothound sharks for the flake market, and they’re taking out more Smooth-hound than any other fishing sector
Chris “The main reason these smaller sharks are disappearing is fishing and particularly shark long lining where thousands of hooks are set over long distances. Each boat is bringing back well over a thousand sharks. Up to thirty-five thousand of just one species are being caught essentially by two at most, three boats along our coastline.
Script: Based in Mosselbay Dr Enrico Gennari started out studying shark movement, but so many tagged shark were getting caught by the shark long liners
Enrico “A colleague of mine in Port Elizabeth which tagged 30s smooth hound sharks and within one month one of those boats caught 27 out of the 30. That's 90 percent 90 percent in one month, one boat
Script: They're easy to target because they congregate in specific areas, feeding alongside endangered shark species like hammerheads and great whites, which are also being hauled in. This boat was caught red handed poaching in the De Hoop marine reserve.
Enrico “There's no record of for example any Hammerhead. Even though there's plenty of footage of them catching hammerhead and then throwing them sometimes out of board. We alerted the inspectors in Mosselbay and they had two days to get to that harbour. Yet nobody was there to check it the landing of that boat. So we know that the protected species are caught but zero record on the files of the department
Leo “So in Australia there's no legal obligation to actually call any form of shark meat by its species so a fish and chip shop can actually call hammerhead shark, it can call bronze whaler flake, there is no legal obligation to call it otherwise. And this is particularly problematic especially when you run the risk of endangered species potentially entering the trade and Australians unwittingly eating them.
Script: Gummy sharks were overfished in Australia, so now they’re protected through strictly enforced quotas. Our Fisheries scientists warned there was 99% probability that sharkfin had already been overfished in 2016, and Smoothhound unsustainably fished.
Link: The department's own scientists are recommending drastic measures are needed and even then it will take up to 50 years for these stocks to recover. Despite making these recommendations since 2011 nothing has actually been put in place
Script: It’s still open season, demersal shark long liners are still allowed to catch as much as they like and everything from the babies to the breeding adults. A slot limit is a management tool to regulate the size of fish caught to protect the breeding stock, but it was never implemented.
Script: Acting DDG for Fisheries Sue Middelton says for the last 10 years Fisheries was split between two different ministries. Just before lockdown they were consolidated into one Department, which she hopes will make the regulatory framework easier
Derek “The slot limit was proposed in 2011 and it was formally adopted in 2015 and even gazetted but it still has not implemented
Sue “It requires an amendment to the permit conditions and to do that, we are required to do socio economic impact assessments.
Derek” But this is almost a decade later. Now they have been filmed fishing in the De Hoop Marine protected area and evidence supplied to the Department why have they not been taken off the sea
Sue “I can confirm, Derek, that two vessels, the White Rose and the Prince Willem have been arrested and prosecuted for fishing in the De Hoop fishery. So those cases are pending.
Script: The Shark diving industry has been hard hit with the disappearance of the Great Whites, and it’s had a knock on effect in the tourist industry. They argue that the demersal shark long liners only employ about 250 people and one small fishery is destroying not only the environment, but hundreds of local jobs
Chris “The great white shark tourism industry alone is worth over one billion rand demersal shark fishing is worth less than 15 million rand so 1.5 percent the value of keeping these animals alive. So this one fishery employing very few people is having a massive detrimental effect the whole way along the coastline.
Script: The public outcry is mounting with over 10 000 signatures on a petition calling for the removal of shark longliners. Even the shore anglers are concerned says Ferdie Botha of the Eastern Province Shore Angling Association, which runs extensive competitions annually
Ferdie “In the past, these sharks comprised of 80 percent of our catches, whereas now it's less than 10 percent
Script: They so concerned they now catch and release sharks
Ferdie “we've gone to great lengths in minimizing the stress levels on these fish. …and to replace them back into the water as soon as possible.
Derek “ What 'm saying is that the numbers of those sharks are declined as your own scientists will tell you. So why are we still feeding the Australians?
Sue “Laugh because we are implementing the upper precautionary limit and on that basis, it's not illegal to catch sharks or export sharks.
Derek “Tell us exactly what’s going to happen when these permits are reissued.
Sue “These permit conditions will be amended after May to introduce the slot limits including the mandatory observer program. The fishing rights are due for re-allocation by December 2021. By that time, the department will have to take a decision on whether to re-allocate fishing rights for a 15 year period, and if so to how many operators
Script: Emotions are running high in the small town of Gansbaai, where the conflict around sharks recently come to a head. Once the White shark mecca with 85 000 trips annually, now down to 20 000. Marine biologist Mary Rowlinson, says everything changed when the Bronze Whaler sharks arrived, they are smaller inquisitive sharks and keep returning
Mary “The Bronze whalers have saved the shark cage diving industry completely because in 2017, when they showed up about a month later, our great white sharks disappeared.
Link: In Gansbaai there is a standoff between the line fishermen who can legally catch bronze whaler sharks and the shark cage diving operators. With the disappearance of the Great Whites it's the Bronze whalers that have helped to sustain the industry
Script: But fishermen were catching massive bronze whaler sharks in front of tourists , which really upset them, so the shark cage operators made a deal with local Gansbaai fishermen, paying them to not catch bronze whalers where they operated, explains Brenda Du Toit
Brenda “From about 27 fishermen, it became something like 84. More fishermen started asking for funding. Bearing In mind every fisherman that was negotiated with signed a contract gave us details of their permits. But over 3 years we are almost at R900 000
Script: But then boats from Cape Town arrived threatening to take out the Bronze whalers, unless they were compensated
Brenda “So 2018 we had fishermen that went out there and in front of tourists started killing Bronze whalers even though they had agreed not to, 2019 similar happened. And again, it happened more recently
Script: They estimate there’re about 200 resident bronze whalers, and when the last fishing trip took out 40, things erupted. We tried to speak to the Gansbaai fishermen, but were met with a lot of aggression, so we approached Wally Croome head of the Commercial Linefishing Association
Wally “Their take on this whole matter is the shark cage people want to work them out of Gansbaai and they are now affecting their livelihood. The shark cage guys are using the media, social media to build up animosity towards the fishermen both locally and internationally
Script: A bronze whaler will fetch about R1000 for a fishermen
Brenda “This is less, way less than 10 percent of their annual income, and it's literally a one-day resource. Whereas the tourism industry is employing over 250 just in Gansbaai alone with a huge amount of benefit. Not to mention the conservation work that the shark industry is supporting, which literally will also come to a grinding halt
Script: They have been asking the Minister for a number of years to declare a shark sanctuary. After several heated meetings they reached an uneasy agreement, to stay 500 meters away from each other, and whoever gets there first, can stay. But once again it all boils down to enforcement, and that’s where things fall apart.
Derek “ And I know it's not your responsibility, but you are protecting a department that really hasn’t done much in the last decade and I can see why people get upset.
Sue “I think under the new department we definitely have a sense of we need to do better. We need to implement it more speedily, science-based decision making has to be paramount
Script And in the meantime, even under lockdown, Australians continue to obliviously eat flake and chips, and we’re wiping out our ocean’s food chain, to supply them.
Leonardo “It’s Quite frankly embarrassing to think that the Australian appetite for Flake has come at the cost of your waters.

Sue “Laugh because we are implementing the upper precautionary limit and on that basis, it's not illegal to catch sharks or export sharks. Derek “Tell us exactly what’s going to happen when these permits are reissued. Sue “These permit conditions will be amended after May to introduce the slot limits including the mandatory observer program. The fishing rights are due for re-allocation by December 2021. By that time, the department will have to take a decision on whether to re-allocate fishing rights for a 15 year period, and if so to how many operators Script: Emotions are running high in the small town of Gansbaai, where the conflict around sharks recently come to a head. Once the White shark mecca with 85 000 trips annually, now down to 20 000. Marine biologist Mary Rowlinson, says everything changed when the Bronze Whaler sharks arrived, they are smaller inquisitive sharks and keep returning Mary “The Bronze whalers have saved the shark cage diving industry completely because in 2017, when they showed up about a month later, our great white sharks disappeared. Link: In Gansbaai there is a standoff between the line fishermen who can legally catch bronze whaler sharks and the shark cage diving operators. With the disappearance of the Great Whites it's the Bronze whalers that have helped to sustain the industry Script: But fishermen were catching massive bronze whaler sharks in front of tourists , which really upset them, so the shark cage operators made a deal with local Gansbaai fishermen, paying them to not catch bronze whalers where they operated, explains Brenda Du Toit Brenda “From about 27 fishermen, it became something like 84. More fishermen started asking for funding. Bearing In mind every fisherman that was negotiated with signed a contract gave us details of their permits. But over 3 years we are almost at R900 000 Script: But then boats from Cape Town arrived threatening to take out the Bronze whalers, unless they were compensated Brenda “So 2018 we had fishermen that went out there and in front of tourists started killing Bronze whalers even though they had agreed not to, 2019 similar happened. And again, it happened more recently Script: They estimate there’re about 200 resident bronze whalers, and when the last fishing trip took out 40, things erupted. We tried to speak to the Gansbaai fishermen, but were met with a lot of aggression, so we approached Wally Croome head of the Commercial Linefishing Association Wally “Their take on this whole matter is the shark cage people want to work them out of Gansbaai and they are now affecting their livelihood. The shark cage guys are using the media, social media to build up animosity towards the fishermen both locally and internationally Script: A bronze whaler will fetch about R1000 for a fishermen Brenda “This is less, way less than 10 percent of their annual income, and it's literally a one-day resource. Whereas the tourism industry is employing over 250 just in Gansbaai alone with a huge amount of benefit. Not to mention the conservation work that the shark industry is supporting, which literally will also come to a grinding halt Script: They have been asking the Minister for a number of years to declare a shark sanctuary. After several heated meetings they reached an uneasy agreement, to stay 500 meters away from each other, and whoever gets there first, can stay. But once again it all boils down to enforcement, and that’s where things fall apart. Derek “ And I know it's not your responsibility, but you are protecting a department that really hasn’t done much in the last decade and I can see why people get upset. Sue “I think under the new department we definitely have a sense of we need to do better. We need to implement it more speedily, science-based decision making has to be paramount Script And in the meantime, even under lockdown, Australians continue to obliviously eat flake and chips, and we’re wiping out our ocean’s food chain, to supply them. Leonardo “It’s Quite frankly embarrassing to think that the Australian appetite for Flake has come at the cost of your waters. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): “Flake and Chips- Aussies take a bite out of our sharks” Sharks are protected in Australia so they importing ours for what they call “flake and chips
metadata.Summary: Demersal long liners are catching sharks, mostly Bronze and Copper sharks but also hammer heads which are protected and exporting them to Australia and Shark Fin mainly to Japan. In 2018 SA exported 113 tons of shark fin to Asia and 56 tons of shark meat. Shark fin is dried before export so you can imagine how many more sharks are being killed. The DEA is not issuing quotas on the number of sharks that fishermen can catch, and despite their own fisheries scientist warning them of the huge drop in numbers the long liners are stripping our waters of shark. 27 of the 30 sharks tagged in PE were caught by a single demersal long line vessel. They have fished out the sharks around PE so have moved to just outside De Hoop Marine protected area. With the demise of the Great Whites, not only due to the Orcas but the demise of the smaller sharks the shark diving tour operators in Gansbaai have paid nearly R1 million rand to local fishermen not catch Bronze/Copper sharks off Gansbaai “watching” zone so they can keep the shark cage diving afloat. But in the last few months this ”deal” has broken down and more and more boats are coming in from Cape Town and catching sharks right in front of tourists. 40 Bronze Whalers were taken out two weeks ago. a month ago fishermen came right up to a shark cage diving boat and caught 4 bronze whaler sharks. A video of 40 smooth-hound sharks and about 12 dozen soupfin sharks and 6 hammerheads was taken just off De Hoop. Sharks reproduce slowly and the copper and hammer heads are listed as endangered species. Over 1 Million sharks are killed annually and not only is this destroying the oceans ecology it’s destroying a local tourist industry, in 2016 we had 85 000 shark cage diving tourist its dropped to below 50 000 now- they say a live shark supports five jobs for every 1 job a dead shark, it’s an industry that employs over 300 local people.
metadata.Further information: Recently the shark cage diving fraternity met with the DEA and shared their research and feel like some progress has been made. But on the other front a dermisal longliner heads back to PE to unload their catch and will be greeted by local inspectors and conservationists - we have a film crew on standby to document it We will also speak to local fishermen who complain about the impact of the longliners and why they resort to catching copper sharks. Covid 19 will impact the local shark cage diving industry massively and Gansbaai operators are concerned that if they are not out on the water the monitoring work they do of the great whites and other sharks will be severely impacted and it will be open season for people who wont be monitored by conservation and shark cage diving operators
metadata.Extra Budget Items: Gansbaai is a 3 hour drive from Cape Town and we have to interview Chris Fallow in Cape Town so will need an additional half day to accommodate the distances
